correctness.rationale: The one-jump decomposition of path variation and constant-reproduction of the orthoprojector reduce the exact nonlinear absolute-value optimization to finitely many step responses. Three sampled orthogonal polynomial norms and their tail moments yield the stated rational gradient formula for every n≥3 and every jump. Exact independent rational Gram inversions agree in 464 cases and check arbitrary rational test vectors. The continuous uniform-L2 polynomial step projection has exact moment coefficients; its piecewise total variation and quartic stationary roots yield a unique maximizing pair up to reflection. Uniform convergence of moment matrices and step moments and continuity of finite-variation for bounded quadratic coefficients prove the limit and localization, not an extrapolation of the tests. The special n=3 case is identity and all limits are bounded.

originality.rationale: Nine actual published-finding corpus semantic searches, full text of the closest three published quadratic-projection records and accessible primary approximation/interpolation literature show no found theorem that implies this specific sharp adjacent-total-variation norm, its attained finite jump formula or its algebraic interior-limit optimizer. The same-grid results bound boundary evaluation rather than variation, and the Jacobi monotone result controls only pointwise range. This is a qualified best-knowledge scientific priority assessment, not proof of uniqueness; unindexed older equivalent theory remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed pre-2009 Gram/discrete-orthogonal polynomial or bounded-variation projection literature may contain equivalent sharp quadratic estimates, despite no identified matching published-finding corpus record.
No exhaustive discovery of every historical dissertation/monograph chapter; absence in searched sources does not prove historical uniqueness.

The discrete all-dimensional rational formula is structurally elementary once the correct BV seminorm is chosen; its mathematical contribution is its sharp joint finite/asymptotic analysis and interior-localization, not the general one-jump decomposition alone.

value.rationale: A natural and commonly used global quadratic least-squares smoother is Euclidean-orthogonal but can amplify total variation of input errors by a sharp and dimension-independent limiting factor ≈1.63318. The exact rational all-n formula and attained extremal jump data provide concrete stability thresholds, while the algebraic limit and two interior maximizing jump locations reveal a geometrically nontrivial boundary-versus-interior effect not supplied by classic pointwise endpoint bounds. It distinguishes true variation sensitivity from mere coordinatewise overshoot for discontinuous data and has direct use in assessing reconstruction stability.
